papers.title: June 2023 · A-Level Biology A Paper 2: Energy, Exercise and Coordination

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Identifying the mitosis stage involving spindle fibres.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing recall of the order of events in mitosis.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits identifying metaphase as the stage at which spindle fibres join the centromeres, with the other stages rejected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Nuclear envelope breakdown stage.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing straightforward recall of mitosis stages.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits prophase as the stage at which the nuclear envelope begins to break down, rejecting interphase, metaphase and telophase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Identifying when chromatids first appear in dividing cells.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Recall of mitosis stages linked to what is visible under a light microscope, with one mark available.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits prophase as the first stage at which chromatids can be seen, rejecting interphase, metaphase and telophase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Crossing over and variation.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark explanation requiring recall of crossing over and a link to the resulting variation, in a familiar context.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits swapping of alleles between non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair, giving new combinations of alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Spotting the true comparison of bacterial and human DNA.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing recall of DNA structure in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the statement that the sugar in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic DNA is deoxyribose, rejecting the three false comparisons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Explaining the term for a co-regulated gene group.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark definition requiring recall of a specification term.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits an operon as a group of genes or section of DNA controlled by a single operator or promoter and transcribed together.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Lactose effect on gene expression.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark description requiring recall of the lac operon sequence of events in an expected prokaryote context.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits lactose allowing the lac operon to function, RNA polymerase binding, transcription and production of lactose-metabolising enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Recalling what a knee ligament is made of and does.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing recall of connective tissue structure and function.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.1.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the ligament being elastic and attaching bone to bone, rejecting options that give muscle attachment or non-elastic structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Age pattern in surgery.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark comment on a stacked chart needing description of overall trends and comparison between groups, with no calculation.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.14.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits little change over time for each age group, the 20-29 group highest and the 50+ group lowest, and a decrease with age.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Completing a table ratio to one significant figure.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-step calculation with a given pattern in the table and a rounding requirement.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the ratio 0.005 : 1, from dividing 68 by 13 472 and giving one significant figure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Infection risk by surgery type.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark application of infection and wound ideas to an unfamiliar surgical context, needing a short reasoned link.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 6.11, 7.14.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits a larger opening and slower recovery giving pathogens more access and time to enter, with the converse allowed for keyhole surgery.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Comparing two prenatal genetic screening methods.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Four-mark compare and contrast needing recall of two screening methods and an organised similarity and differences answer.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits both tests looking for genetic conditions, with differences in timing relative to implantation, miscarriage risk and what material is tested.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Social issues of PGD.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark description of social issues from recall of the specification, with no data to handle.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits two social issues such as selecting one embryo over another, selecting for other characteristics, or cost and emotional strain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Cystic fibrosis and digestion.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark explanation linking a genetic condition to its effect on a body system, needing application beyond straight recall.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits thick sticky mucus blocking the pancreatic duct or bile duct so that digestive secretions are reduced and digestion is reduced.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Scaling an image up to a molecule's true size.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark multi-step calculation involving magnification, unit conversion and standard form.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits calculating the bacterial width from the image, dividing by 250 for the DNA width and giving the answer in standard form in micrometres.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Predicting DNA strand patterns after growth in light nitrogen.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark table completion requiring prediction of outcomes for two models from knowledge of the Meselson and Stahl approach.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the expected heavy and light strand combinations for conservative and semi-conservative replication, before and after each replication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Explaining the mechanism shown by the Meselson-Stahl results.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark explanation of a named term, needing recall of the replication mechanism.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits doubling of the DNA, each original strand acting as a template, and each new molecule holding one old and one new strand.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Effect on clotting time.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark application of the clotting cascade to an unfamiliar infection, needing a sequenced explanation.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits less thromboplastin, slower conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and fibrinogen to fibrin, and fewer platelets trapped in the mesh.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Naming other outputs of the first respiration stage.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark recall of glycolysis products.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.4.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits reduced NAD and ATP as the other products of glycolysis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Predicting the fate of a metabolite when a pathway stops.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark application of respiration pathways to a hypothetical change in a diagram, rather than direct recall.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.4, 7.7.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the three-carbon molecule being used in anaerobic respiration, accepting hydrogen from reduced NAD and forming lactate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Choosing the carbon pattern for the cycle in a diagram.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing recall of how carbon numbers change in the Krebs cycle.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.5.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits option D, a six-five-four carbon sequence, with the others rejected because carbons are recycled in the Krebs cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Explaining liquid movement in a maggot respirometer.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark explanation of a respirometer result needing a short chain of reasoning in a practical context.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.3, CP16.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits oxygen being used, carbon dioxide being absorbed by potassium hydroxide, and so a fall in pressure or volume in the tube.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Planning a temperature investigation using a respirometer.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Five-mark open design task requiring the candidate to plan a controlled respirometer investigation with several practical features.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 5.16, CP12, CP16.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits a suitable temperature range, a controlled variable, measuring liquid movement, a judgement of the optimum, set-up detail and repeats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Why endurance runners need a mix of muscle fibre types.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Five-mark explanation applying muscle fibre data to the demands of an endurance athlete, requiring several linked advantages.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.10, 7.4.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits more slow-twitch fibres for fatigue resistance and aerobic respiration, balanced by some fast-twitch fibres for a faster finish.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Checking three statements about gene therapy methods.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice requiring evaluation of three statements about gene therapy techniques.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.17.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits none of the three statements being correct, with ligase, restriction enzymes and the vector each misused.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Counting bonds cut when a DNA fragment is released.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark reasoning from a short DNA diagram, needing the idea that both strands are cut at each end.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.17.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits four phosphodiester bonds hydrolysed to release the fragment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Why a treated patient could still have an affected child.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark multi-step explanation applying genetics to an unfamiliar treatment scenario.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.17.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits modification only in eye cells, gametes still carrying the recessive allele, and a partner also supplying a recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Choosing what makes medicines tailored to individuals possible.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark multiple choice needing recall of a Human Genome Project outcome.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.16.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits differences in the genome between people as the basis for personalised medicine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: ATP in impulse transmission.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark explanation needing recall of the resting potential mechanism and a link to ATP.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.3.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits ATP for sodium-potassium pumps moving ions against concentration gradients to maintain the potential difference across the axon membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Explaining how myosin could carry organelles along actin.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark application of the muscle contraction mechanism to an unfamiliar context of organelle transport.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 7.2.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits the myosin head attaching to actin, acting as an ATPase to split ATP, and changing position to move the mitochondrion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Calculating organelle travel time along a long axon.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark multi-step calculation needing unit conversions across length and time.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits converting 9 cm to micrometres, dividing by the speed to get seconds, and converting to hours to give 50.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Discussing lipid and protein roles in two nerve cell membranes.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Six-mark levels-marked extended discussion requiring data from the table to be linked to membrane structure and the functions of two cell types.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.1, 8.3.
provenance.tag_basis: Indicative content covers phospholipid bilayer barriers, lipids in the myelin sheath and saltatory conduction, and channel and carrier proteins in neurone action potentials.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Working out how many pedigree members have known genotypes.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-mark pedigree interpretation requiring careful reasoning about each individual.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits nine as the number of individuals whose genotype can be determined from the pedigree.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Linking a gene mutation to altered light absorbance.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark explanation linking gene mutation to protein structure, applied to unfamiliar absorbance data.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.5.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits a mutation changing the amino acid sequence of opsin, altering tertiary structure and so shifting the absorbance ratio.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Rod cell and bipolar neurone.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Four-mark multi-step description of visual signalling in an unfamiliar context, with the conclusion running opposite to expectation.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.4, 8.5.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits sodium ions entering the rod cell in the dark, depolarisation, glutamate release and inhibition of depolarisation in the bipolar neurone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Describing how a plant pigment controls flowering.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark description requiring recall of phytochrome conversion applied to long-day plants.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.6.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits red phytochrome converting to far-red form in long days, with accumulated far-red form stimulating flowering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Designing a test for day-length response in plants.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Three-mark investigation design needing identification of the independent variable, a control and a measured outcome.
provenance.year_basis: Requires Year 13 content (Topics 5–8 or their core practicals): 8.6.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits varying the hours of light per day, controlling another abiotic factor and recording whether plants flower.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Calculating the proportion of fat that is unsaturated.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Single-step percentage calculation requiring the unsaturated mass to be worked out from the table.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits dividing the unsaturated fat mass by total fat and multiplying by 100 to give about 38%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Biscuits to exceed sugar limit.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-step calculation combining division of table values with rounding to a whole number.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits sugar mass per biscuit from the four-biscuit value and dividing the recommended intake by it to get 18 biscuits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Working back to a daily energy allowance in joules.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-step calculation involving a percentage reversal, unit conversion and standard form.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits scaling 700 kJ by 100 divided by 8 and converting to joules in standard form as 8.75 x 10^6.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Age BMI effects on CHD.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Two-mark description of trends in a data table, requiring comparison of two variables.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Scheme credits CHD incidence rising with increasing age and BMI, with age having the greater effect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.preview_text: Evaluating CHD risk factors.

provenance.difficulty_basis: Six-mark levels-marked evaluation synthesising a table and three graphs to reach a justified conclusion.
provenance.year_basis: Every tagged statement is Topics 1–4 (Year 12) content or a mathematical skill.
provenance.tag_basis: Indicative content covers study design limits, differing time spans of the data, and comparing the effects of age, BMI, smoking, inactivity and alcohol on CHD.
